title: Recording: Heart On My Sleeve, Where Did Our Love Go, Tonight, A Man Like Me by Ringo Starr | 1978
content:
Warner Bros Studios, Los Angeles
Producer: Vini Poncia
Engineer: Bob Schaper

Ringo Starr finished recording four songs for his seventh studio album, Bad Boy, on 8 March 1978.

‘Heart On My Sleeve’ was written by Scottish duo Gallagher & Lyle, and originally released on their fifth studio album, 1976’s Breakaway. Starr’s version was issued as a single in the US on 6 July 1978, with ‘Who Needs A Heart’ on the b-side.

‘Where Did Our Love Go’ was a better-known cover. It was written by Holland-Dozier-Holland, and originally recorded by The Supremes, becoming their first US number one single in 1964.

‘Tonight’ had been written by Ian McLagan and John Pidgeon. McLagan was a member of The Small Faces, and the song appeared on their fourth studio album, 1977’s Playmates. McLagan offered the song to Starr, who repaid the favour by performing on McLagan’s debut solo album, 1979’s Troublemaker.

Starr’s version of ‘Tonight’ became the only UK single taken from Bad Boy. It was released on 21 July 1978 but failed to reach the singles chart.

‘A Man Like Me’ was a reworking of the Scouse The Mouse song ‘A Mouse Like Me’ with amended lyrics – the word “mouse” was simply changed to “man”.
